top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Florida. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 101 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Florida's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
At mile 60 of 101, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Gran Fondo Florida's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Florida. Train it until it feels boring.
At Gran Fondo Florida, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Florida. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,409ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 101 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
101 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.weather: March in Dade City, Florida, USA. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Florida. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Florida’s 101 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Florida rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 101 miles of mixed terrain in Dade City, Florida, USA.
